findings.title: String#ends_with? does not exist; NoMethodError in the else branch
findings.body: In the `website_name` method, the fallback branch calls `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. Ruby's String method is `end_with?`; the `ends_with?`/`starts_with?` aliases were provided by old ActiveSupport versions and were removed in Rails 4, which this codebase runs on. Whenever a user's website host is a parent domain of the instance hostname (e.g. website `example.com` on instance `forums.example.com`), serializing the user will raise NoMethodError and the whole user JSON endpoint will 500. This also means the third new spec (`returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain`) would fail if run, so the tests appear not to have been executed. Change to `end_with?`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix, so the guard is never invoked
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers only honors inclusion guards named `include_<attribute>?`. The method here is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, including a `website_name: null` key for users with no website. If the intent is to suppress the attribute when the website is blank, rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users to anonymous visitors
findings.body: The serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio, location, etc.) from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users via `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, and its inclusion guard only checks `website.present?` — so an anonymous visitor requesting a TL0 user's JSON now receives `website_name` (the website's host, and when it matches the instance domain, the full path) even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the purpose of hiding the website field. `website_name` should be included in `untrusted_attributes` (or its include guard should check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).

findings.title: No test for the same-length subdomain branch of website_name
findings.body: The new `website_name` logic has three branches, but the specs only cover two: different domains and exact/parent-domain matches. The middle branch (equal label counts greater than two, e.g. website `www.example.com` vs instance `forum.example.com`, comparing the domains after stripping the first label) is untested, including its negative case where the registrable domains differ (`www.other.com` vs `forum.example.com`) and only the host should be returned.
